page: Microsoft Azure DC32ds_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the DDCSv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 2458 GB local disk and supports Premium Storage. There are no GPUs on this instance.

Benchmark results show strong performance in multi-core and cryptographic workloads. The server achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 17264.0 and a Passmark CPU extended instructions test score of 53627.12, both placing in the top 25%. Cryptographic capabilities are highlighted by a Passmark CPU encryption score of 36927.97. Database operations are also highly efficient, with a Passmark database score of 25047.25. Static web serving throughput is measured at 48.38 GB/sec. However, text generation for large language models is a notable bottleneck, with the 70B model text generation speed falling into the bottom 25% at 2.64 tokens/sec.

Given the high memory-to-core ratio of 1:8 and the inclusion of a substantial 2458 GB local storage disk, this server offers a resource-dense profile suitable for memory-intensive and database workloads. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without resource contention. It is highly suited for relational databases, memory-cached applications, data processing pipelines, and static web serving. It is less optimal for large-scale LLM text generation due to the lack of GPU acceleration and lower multi-threaded text generation throughput.
